subject: Dedicated capacity: MAP & pricing for GPU pool reservation
messages:
From: Anil Shah <anil.shah@pinecrest.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@pinecrest.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluating Dedicated for latency-sensitive features / need MAP

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the low-p99 latency looked promising for the live inference we need. We're preparing an internal evaluation plan (3-month pilot) for the recommender + search augmentation features and Procurement asked me to request a written MAP (mutual action plan) that ties milestones to commercial triggers.

High-level asks from our side:
- Baseline GPU pool sizing recommendation for the pilot (expected 3–5 rps per model, two models concurrently).
- Clear milestone definitions (pilot start, quality gate, production ramp) and what commercial commitments follow each milestone.
- Pricing for a 12-month reserved pool vs a 3-month pilot + commitment convert option.
- Burst rules and surcharge model if we exceed reserved throughput during peak campaigns.

Can you share a MAP draft and a ballpark pricing sheet so Procurement can scope the PO and timeline? We need internal sign-off by mid-Sept to hit our Q4 launch window.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

— Anil
Head of ML Engineering
Pinecrest AI
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anil Shah <anil.shah@pinecrest.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Evaluating Dedicated for latency-sensitive features / need MAP

Anil — great to hear, and glad the demo was useful. Attached is a first-pass MAP that maps the 3-month evaluation to commercial milestones plus a pricing workbook for both pilot and committed-reserve options.

Quick summary of what you'll see in the MAP (attached):
1) Pilot window (0–90 days): Redwood provides a 2-GPU baseline pool sized for two concurrent 8GB models (est. 3–5 rps each) with prefix caching enabled. No commitment required during pilot.
2) Quality gate (day 45): If model perf meets your eval metrics (p95 latency < 120ms and recall targets), an optional conversion window opens to sign a Reserved Capacity agreement.
3) Commit tiers: 12-month and 24-month term options. Discounts scale with committed vCPU/GPU hours and annualized commit.
4) Burst policy: default burst allowance up to 1.25x of reserved throughput for short windows (daily peaks) with no surcharge; sustained burst (more than 1 hour) billed at a blended overage rate. We included alternate language for a 1.5x early-burst credit if you commit before pilot end.

Attachments: Pinecrest-MAP-v1.pdf (MAP draft), pricing-dedicated-20260901.xlsx (line-item pricing by GPU type).

Ben (CC'd) will own commercial framing; Monica will handle technical sizing. If you want, let's schedule a 30-min alignment Thursday to walk the MAP and the pricing assumptions. Mid-Sept sign-off sounds doable if we move quickly.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Evaluating Dedicated for latency-sensitive features / need MAP

Anil — quick technical note on sizing and burst behavior based on the workload you described.

Baseline recommendation (pilot):
- 2x A10G-equivalent GPUs in a shared pool, continuous batching enabled, KV prefix cache warmup during first 24–48 hours. This should cover the 3–5 rps per model estimate with headroom for 1.2x typical variance.

If you expect marketing campaign spikes (5–10x short bursts):
- Short bursts (under 30 minutes): we can leverage autoscale burst capacity to 2x reserved throughput with no immediate surcharge if average over a 24-hour window stays within threshold.
- Sustained bursts (>1 hour): billed as overage. Suggested approach: allow 1.5x free burst credit for the first 90 days of pilot to smooth go-live risk, then revert to the standard burst surcharge (pricing sheet includes blended rates).

Operational notes:
- We recommend instrumenting the prefix cache hooks and the Redwood Console dashboards during pilot so we can open a performance tuning window at day 21.
- If you plan to run larger models or add a third concurrent model, budget for an additional GPU or model-variant quantization.

I've annotated the attached pricing workbook with the expected per-hour overage rates and a sample monthly cost schedule for 12- and 24-month terms.

— Monica
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
Attachments: pricing-dedicated-20260901.xlsx (annotated), SOW-Pinecrest-draft.docx (initial SOW skeleton)
From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@pinecrest.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anil Shah <anil.shah@pinecrest.ai>, Procurement <procurement@pinecrest.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Sep 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Evaluating Dedicated for latency-sensitive features / need MAP

Marissa / team — thanks for the MAP and detailed notes. A few items Procurement/legal want clearer before we commit to internal approvals: 

1) Commit flexibility: our ops team wants a staircase commit (start at 2 GPUs, add second tranche at month 4) rather than an immediate full reserve. Can you provide pricing for a staged commit?
2) Burst surcharge: the current overage model looks punitive for campaign-heavy months. Can you propose a mechanism that caps maximum monthly surcharge (e.g., no more than 25% over the reserved spend) or a blended cap?
3) Discount tie to MAP outcomes: we like the idea of a conversion discount if we sign before pilot end. Can that be an explicit line item (e.g., 12% off list for 12-month term if signed within 60 days of pilot start)?

Attached: redlines-pricing.xlsx with our proposed staircase and surcharge cap. We want to get to commercial terms this month.

— Rajiv
VP, Business Ops
Pinecrest AI
Attachments: redlines-pricing.xlsx (procurement suggested edits)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Evaluating Dedicated for latency-sensitive features / need MAP

Rajiv / Anil — appreciate the direct redlines, and happy to find common ground. Proposal below (commercial compromise to unblock procurement this month):

- Staged commit (staircase): 12-month term, start at 2 GPUs (tranche A). Tranche B (add 1 extra GPU) automatically becomes billable at month 4 unless you notify us 30 days prior to cancel; pricing for Tranche B is 80% of list per-GPU hour when added within the first 6 months.

- Burst policy (simplified cap): up to 1.25x reserved throughput free for daily peaks. For sustained bursts beyond 1 hour, overage applied, but capped such that monthly overage charges do not exceed 25% of the reserved monthly spend (for the first 6 months). After month 6, standard overage rates apply without the cap.

- Conversion discount: if Pinecrest signs a 12-month reserved agreement within 60 days of pilot start, Redwood will apply a 12% discount to the committed base spend (applies to both tranche A and tranche B if tranche B is accepted within the 60-day window).

- SLA and credit: p95 latency SLO of 150ms with service credits up to 5% for missed monthly SLOs.

Next steps: I'll upload the commercial term sheet to DocuSign for an initial sign-off and loop in Legal for a short-form addendum. If this all looks OK, please confirm by EOD Monday and we'll send the DocuSign link.
